page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between compute power and memory capacity. The shared AMD EPYC processor delivers poor single-core performance, scoring 787.09 in stress-ng tests, and weak multi-core performance at 3134.25. Memory bandwidth is average for small cached blocks at 411.75 GB/sec, but drops to a weak 35.68 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Passmark CPU tests show average capabilities in extended instructions and encryption, while database operations and Redis SET throughput remain in the lower performance tier.

Given its shared CPU architecture and high memory density, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance compute. It is well-suited for caching layers, lightweight database replicas, and memory-heavy background processing. However, it is less optimal for CPU-bound tasks, high-throughput web serving, or large-scale LLM inference.
